text:
maria: Heads-up — I put together a quick heatmap of Xid/ECC bursts across regions for the last 48h. eu-west1 shows a dense cluster around rack3/slot 12 that correlates with higher preemptions.
monitor-bot: [auto] suspicious spike: nvidia_xid_errors_total increased by 643 in eu-west1 (48h).
sam: can you paste the grafana panel query so I can reuse it in the incident dashboard?
maria: sure — this is what I used for the per-card burst panel:
```
sum by (card, region) (increase(nvidia_xid_errors_total[30m]))
```
lee: that looks good. threshold we should alert on? current noise makes 1-min alerts terrible.
jordan: propose two-tier rules: warn if >50 errors in 30m, critical if >200 in 30m, both with a 15m "for" to avoid flapping. also add cardinality cap per-card so it doesn't blow up for high-card fleets.
maria: agreed on thresholds. also adding arolling median baseline per card helps — if a card is 10x its baseline we flag it.
sam: +1. can we also surface the kv-cache hit rate and network drops on the same row so ops can correlate?
maria: yep — added panels for: kernel_oops_count, net_drops_total, kv_cache_miss_ratio. stack them by region and rack.
lee: one more thought — rather than immediate drain, we should use a "quarantine" state: pin new allocs away from the card for 24h and only drain if errors persist. reduces churn and spare usage.
jordan: that ties into cost tradeoffs — draining and replacing a whole node costs ~1200USD in spare capacity during rotation for a 4-GPU host for 48h. quarantine is cheaper but risks impacting tail-latency if the card degrades further. we need an eviction budget.
maria: proposal: per-region eviction budget 1.5% of cards, auto-escalate to ops when nearing budget. add a grafana panel showing budget usage and projected depletion.
sam: for SLOs: define card-level availability SLO as 99.95% per region (monthly window). if a region dips below 99.9% for two consecutive days, trigger capacity rebalancing and a postmortem.
lee: ok — rolling alert actions: 1) quarantine pin, 2) 2x-retry at lower batch size, 3) if error rate still >critical for 24h -> schedule drain/replace.
maria: I'm going to open a PR to grafana-dashboards with: 1) heatmap panel grouped by (region, rack), 2) per-card sparkline with baseline overlay, 3) eviction-budget gauge, 4) composite correlation row (Xid vs net drops vs temp).
maria: sample panel json snippet for the heatmap to include in the PR:
```
{"type":"heatmap","targets":[{"expr":"sum by (card) (increase(nvidia_xid_errors_total[30m]))","legendFormat":"{{card}}"}],"options":{"color":{"mode":"spectrum"},"yBucketSize":"auto"}}
```
jordan: ping @sam for runbook link — we should attach the drain playbook to the alert.
sam: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-drain-replace — added to alert annotations. also I'll add a small doc section on when to pick proactive replacement vs quarantine.
monitor-bot: [auto] grafana-dashboards repo: PR #789 opened by maria: "gpu/xid-heatmap + eviction budget panel". CI: lint OK.
lee: I'll review the PR today and add the cardinality guard. can we set a per-panel limit of 500 series to avoid exploding queries?
maria: yep — limiting to topk(500, ...) in the query and adding a fallback summary metric.
jordan: final checklist before merge: 1) add 15m for() on alerts, 2) link runbook, 3) include cost estimate in PR description, 4) add annotation for "last known good" snapshot.
sam: I can estimate replacement cost and put numbers in the PR (including spare reservation and cross-region routing cost).
maria: cool — thanks. I'm going to push the dashboard changes and the baseline calc. if anyone sees a missing metric, ping here. :thumbsup:
